summary:
ARES (Advanced Martian Exploration & Survival System) is an intelligent Mars exploration and mission-planning platform designed to support safer and more efficient human exploration of Mars. It integrates scientific data from multiple NASA missions into a unified interactive Martian GIS environment.

ARES features an interactive Mars map with scientific layers such as MOLA elevation, THEMIS thermal imagery, HiRISE and CTX surface imagery. Its Terrain Intelligence module provides elevation analysis, slope assessment and terrain visualization, while Hazard Intelligence helps identify potentially dangerous and uncertain regions.

The Marswalk Route Planner enables users to select destinations, compare routes, assess terrain risks and balance astronaut safety with scientific exploration. Environmental Intelligence presents available observations of temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind and dust conditions.

The platform also includes a NASA Science Explorer for accessing planetary imagery and datasets, and a Mission Report Generator for organizing exploration routes, terrain assessments, hazards and scientific findings.

By combining planetary GIS, NASA scientific data, terrain intelligence and route optimization, ARES aims to transform complex Martian information into actionable insights for future astronauts, enabling safer exploration and more productive scientific discoveries on Mars.
details:
ARES – Advanced Martian Exploration & Survival System

ARES is an intelligent Mars exploration and mission-planning platform designed to support safer and more efficient human exploration of Mars. It combines scientific datasets from multiple NASA missions into a unified interactive Martian GIS environment.

The platform allows users to explore Mars through interactive maps, examine surface imagery, investigate elevation and terrain characteristics, identify potential hazards, and plan exploration routes. Its key features include a Martian GIS Explorer, Terrain Intelligence, Hazard Intelligence, Marswalk Route Planner, Environmental Intelligence, NASA Science Explorer, and Mission Report Generator.

ARES benefits future astronauts and mission planners by bringing fragmented planetary data into one accessible platform. It aims to help users make informed decisions, reduce potential terrain-related risks, identify scientifically valuable locations, and plan more productive exploration missions.

The intended impact is to support future human missions to Mars by transforming complex scientific information into practical exploration insights, improving mission preparation, and encouraging safer surface exploration.

The project uses modern web technologies, including Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, OpenLayers, Recharts, and Framer Motion. NASA, JPL, USGS, and Planetary Data System resources are intended as scientific data sources. GitHub is used for version control, and Vercel for deployment.

ARES is creative because it brings planetary GIS, scientific visualization, hazard assessment, and route optimization together in a single mission-planning experience rather than treating them as separate tools.

Our team considered scientific accuracy, astronaut safety, terrain uncertainty, data availability, usability, performance, accessibility, and scalability while designing the project.
